checks.detail: code 1.565694 = 2 - N_i/N. The BEQ/BEB alternative would be 2 - Q = 1.4332 (Kim & Rudd eq. 60). These are DIFFERENT MODELS; eq. (20) is the one with D(t), and it takes N_i/N. Using 2 - Q here would be an error of 8.5%.
checks.name: non-dipole coefficient is [2 - N_i/N] (eq. 20), not [2 - Q]

checks.detail: max relative difference over t = 1.5 ... 1e6 is 2.12e-16. The code's Horner form is the analytic integral of the Table I polynomial.
checks.name: D(t) closed form in the code == numerical quadrature of eq. (56)

checks.detail: max relative difference over 15 eV - 1 GeV is 1.41e-09, which is the level of the independently sourced constants (the code builds the prefactor from its own r_e, this check from a_0 and alpha). The code implements RBED (eq. 20), which uses the true D(t) -- NOT RBEB (eq. 22).
checks.name: coll_ionisation_cross_section == Kim 2000 eq. (20), reimplemented

checks.detail: total from the DIFFERENTIAL formula agrees with the closed form to 4.67e-05 -- an independent check of both.
checks.name: eq. (20) is the integral of eq. (19), as the paper states

checks.detail: swapping the NIST binding energy for Kim's tabulated Rydberg changes the RBED cross section by at most 0.225% over 20 eV - 1 GeV. It is a REAL inconsistency -- the Table I fit, M^2, N_i and the (R/B)^2 in S were all derived with B = R -- but it is below every other uncertainty here, and it is redshift-INDEPENDENT, so it cancels from any z=10 / z=20 comparison.
checks.name: the B ambiguity is bounded and small

checks.detail: n_HI, n_H, T_CMB, u_CMB and B(z) all reproduce their stated powers of (1+z) to better than 5.6e-16. Measured by evaluating the code at both redshifts, not by reading the source.
checks.name: every analytic z-scaling in the code is the one the equations state

checks.detail: the gap vanishes at z=0 (|-2.2e-16|) and is proportional to (1+z) over z=5..30: gap/(1+z) = 1.1968e-04..1.2893e-04, a spread of only 7.4%. That is the signature of an Omega_r (1+z)^4 term missing from under the square root, with an implied Omega_r = 2*slope*Omega_m = 7.78e-05 -- the right order for photons plus the relativistic part of the neutrino background (Omega_gamma = 5.4e-5). CONSEQUENCE: this is not two cosmologies and not a coding error. Route 1 drops a term that grows as (1+z), which is exactly why the gap DOUBLES from 1.369e-03 at z=10 to 2.675e-03 at z=20. Route 2 (astropy Planck18), which the yield actually uses, is the complete one. The earlier 'pending decision' is therefore settled on physics: the yield already uses the better H(z).
checks.name: the route-1 / route-2 H(z) gap is a missing relativistic term

checks.detail: sigma_ion at 100 eV / 1 keV / 1 MeV is bit-identical at z=10 and z=20: 5.783777e-21, 1.249236e-21, 9.913644e-24 m^2. Kim 2000 eq. (20) and Stone & Kim 2002 are ATOMIC physics -- no cosmology enters them. Redshift acts only through the target DENSITY n_HI(z), which multiplies them. This is why the yield below ~10 keV is z-invariant: every competing channel there is collisional and carries the same n_HI, which cancels from the branching ratio.
checks.name: RBED and the excitation cross sections are redshift-independent

checks.detail: b = 4 gamma kT/mc^2 is the Klein-Nishina parameter; the Thomson limit needs b << 1. Over the channel window (2e7-3e8 eV at z=20) b stays below 2.27e-05, so BG70 eq. (2.42) is valid there at BOTH redshifts.Already checked independently as F_KN = 0.99999/0.99986 at the 5%/95% points of the z=20 window. At the top of the grid, 1e12 eV, b rises to 0.076 at z=20 against 0.040 at z=10 -- still below unity, so the Thomson spectrum is marginal rather than invalid there (a few per cent), and the LOSS rate uses the full KN kernel at every energy regardless.
checks.name: Thomson limit still holds for the IC-secondary channel at z=20

checks.detail: E_esc = 1218.0 eV at z=10 and 1625.7 eV at z=20, a ratio of 1.3348 against the analytic estimate (1+z)^0.5 = 1.3817 (3.4% from it, the residual being the energy dependence of sigma_pi departing from a pure E^-3). It is solved from tau(E) at the requested redshift, NOT held at its z=10 value -- so the IC-secondary window shifts correctly. The prose '~1.2 keV' in the code comments and '~1.4 keV' in ionization_yield.py are z=10 statements and should not be read as constants.
checks.name: the escape energy is recomputed from z, and moves as predicted

checks.detail: x_e enters only the Coulomb term, whose peak share of dK/dt is 0.23% at z=10 and 0.23% at z=20 (measured, C20 in yield_comparison). Post-recombination freeze-out leaves x_e ~ a few 1e-4 and only falls slowly, so 1e-4 is the same order at z=20 as at z=10. NOT DERIVED HERE and not measured: it is the user's stated value, and the yield is insensitive to it at the 0.2% level either way.
checks.name: x_e = 1e-4 is a defensible constant at BOTH redshifts, but it IS a choice
